title: Kalocsa floral painting
summary: Kalocsa, a market town in southern Hungary, is known for flowers painted in bold red, blue, green and violet. Women paint each petal with one press and lift of a round brush, filling whitewashed walls, furniture and cloth with bouquets, wreaths and friezes.
howToPlay: Look at the flower plan on the card: each bloom, bud and leaf has its own colour.
Dip the brush in a paint, then choose a flower, petal, leaf or dot from the tray.
Touch the wall to paint. The mirror partner on the other side is painted at the same moment.
Press Check to compare your wall with the plan.
rules: The wall is mirrored left to right, so each press is painted in up to two places at once.
A place counts only when both its shape and its paint colour match the plan.
Painting the same shape in the same colour again wipes it off.
Three stars need a near perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Flower painting from Kalocsa grew out of the town's embroidered folk dress and was carried onto house walls, furniture and paprika jars, usually by women of the region. It is counted among Hungary's valued folk arts.
